strengths: Addresses an important and practical challenge in 3D content creation and robotics simulation: synthesizing geometrically compatible, collision-aware interactive multi-object assemblies rather than monolithic, fused meshes.

Well-structured 'generate-then-compose' pipeline that intelligently repurposes 2D/3D generative priors (Nano Banana Pro, TRELLIS2, PartField) into 3D spatial guidance, decoupling individual asset quality from spatial layout.

The two-stage composition mechanism is technically sound, combining global-to-local registration (OBB + GeoTransformer + Scale-aware ICP) with an SDF-based collision-penalty optimization to prevent mesh interpenetration.

The closed-loop agentic refinement is an innovative design: using a VLM to visually diagnose clipping or implausible geometry and iteratively edit the 2D prompt/image to resolve topological conflicts that rigid alignment alone cannot fix.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation across 150 test cases with diverse metrics (CLIP text/image scores, human/VLM evaluations, surface and volumetric intersection rates) against relevant feed-forward and registration baselines, accompanied by the curation of an 8,300-scene compositional dataset.
weaknesses: High computational overhead and latency: The pipeline chains several heavy components (multiple 2D diffusion inferences, 3D feed-forward reconstructions via TRELLIS2, 3D part segmentation, SDF optimization, and up to 5 iterative VLM feedback loops). A clear runtime breakdown and analysis of inference efficiency are missing.

Pipeline fragility and compounding errors: Because each module operates sequentially (2D generation -> 3D reconstruction -> part segmentation -> registration -> refinement), errors or inconsistencies at earlier stages (such as hallucinated occluded geometry or segmentation artifacts) can propagate downstream.

Limited physical realism beyond collision avoidance: The physics formulation primarily penalizes intersection/collision via SDFs, but does not explicitly model static equilibrium, center of mass, gravity/support stability, or contact friction required for physically grounded robotic simulation.

Dataset verification details: The paper introduces an 8,300-scene dataset generated by the automated pipeline, but lacks comprehensive statistics regarding failure filtering, automated validation criteria, or human quality assurance across the full dataset.

strengths: Addresses an important and timely problem: existing 3D generative foundation models produce monolithic, fused meshes lacking independent object-level identities and object-object relationships (OOR), which severely hinders their use in robotic simulation and interaction.

The proposed generate-then-compose pipeline is elegant and training-free, cleverly leveraging spatial guidance from a composite scene to guide the registration and scale alignment of separately generated high-fidelity assets.

The two-stage composition strategy—combining robust global-to-local registration (OBB + GeoTransformer + ICP) with a differentiable SDF-based collision penalty—effectively resolves interpenetration issues.

The closed-loop agentic refinement via VLM visual inspection provides a creative semantic-level corrective mechanism when geometric adjustment alone is insufficient to resolve occlusions or incompatible shapes.

Extensive visual results across diverse categories (including multi-object compositions with >2 parts) and promising quantitative improvements in collision reduction and alignment fidelity compared to existing baselines.
weaknesses: High pipeline complexity and runtime overhead: The framework chains together multiple heavy generative models (2D image editing, TRELLIS2 3D reconstruction, PartField segmentation, GeoTransformer registration, SDF optimization, and up to 5 VLM refinement iterations). The paper lacks runtime and computational cost analysis.

Heavy reliance on 2D editing priors: The pipeline depends fundamentally on the ability of the 2D editing model (Nano Banana Pro / Gemini) to hallucinate occluded geometry and isolate components while preserving viewpoint and consistency. Failures in 2D propagation can directly degrade the 3D pipeline.

Evaluation of 'physical plausibility' is limited to geometric non-penetration: Although the motivation highlights robotic manipulation and Sim2Real simulation, the evaluation only measures surface/volume collision metrics rather than dynamic physical validity (e.g., resting stability under gravity in a physics engine like Isaac Gym or PyBullet).

strengths: Addresses an important and practical challenge in 3D content creation: generating independent, geometrically compatible, and collision-aware interactive multi-object 3D compositions without requiring expensive end-to-end 3D model training.

The two-stage registration pipeline is logically structured, combining global initialization via GeoTransformer, local scale-aware ICP, and a differentiable SDF-based collision penalty to effectively reduce mesh interpenetration.
The inclusion of a VLM-guided agentic refinement loop is an effective strategy to address fundamental geometric mismatches caused by 2D occlusions that cannot be fixed by rigid transformations alone.
Extensive visual demonstrations, including multi-view renderings and multi-object compositions (e.g., shoe cabinet, fruit basket), show compelling visual fidelity.
weaknesses: Technical originality is somewhat limited; the framework is largely an integration and chaining of existing off-the-shelf tools and methods (image generation/editing models, TRELLIS2, PartField, GeoTransformer, and Umeyama/ICP) with a standard SDF-based collision penalty.

Clarity and reproducibility concerns regarding components: The manuscript repeatedly refers to 'Nano Banana Pro [9]' for image editing and generation, citing a generic Google Gemini URL. It is unclear what specific model or API is being used under this name, which impairs experimental reproducibility.

Claims regarding 'physically-sound' and 'interactive' environments are overstated: The physics consideration is limited to rigid pose optimization with an interpenetration penalty. Key physical properties such as contact mechanics, gravity, center of mass, frictional support, and resting stability are not modeled.

Computational cost and latency analysis are omitted: Running multi-turn 2D image generation, multi-asset 3D reconstruction (TRELLIS2), part segmentation, geometric feature matching, SDF optimization, and up to 5 iterative VLM feedback loops appears computationally heavy, yet the inference time and resource footprint per scene are not discussed.

High failure rate: In the analysis of 140 additional cases (Figure 7), approximately 29 cases (~21%) fail due to symmetry ambiguity or collision-induced divergence, highlighting noticeable fragility when handling symmetric or complex geometries.

strengths: Addresses an important and challenging problem in 3D vision and robotics: generating multi-part, geometrically compatible, and collision-free compositional 3D assets.

The proposed generate-then-compose framework smartly leverages 2D image foundation priors (for scene arrangement and object hallucination) and 3D foundation models (TRELLIS2/PartField) as coarse spatial guidance, avoiding end-to-end retraining.

The two-stage composition pipeline, combining global-to-local registration (OBB, GeoTransformer, scale-aware ICP) and differentiable SDF-based collision optimization, is technically sound and directly tackles interpenetration.
The closed-loop agentic refinement mechanism with a VLM effectively resolves fundamental geometric mismatches caused by 2D occlusions that rigid transformations cannot correct.
Qualitative results on both two-part and multi-part compositions are convincing, and the release of an 8,300-scene interactive 3D dataset represents a valuable contribution to the community.
weaknesses: The quantitative evaluation is performed on a very limited set of only 10 test cases (Table 2), which is unusually small given the claim of curating an 8,300-scene dataset. A benchmark over a larger, representative split would provide stronger statistical confidence.

The manuscript lacks rigorous quantitative ablation studies dissecting individual components—such as isolating the quantitative contribution of GeoTransformer initialization, the SDF collision loss schedule, and the agentic VLM feedback iterations.

The pipeline relies on a cascade of heavy models (VLM / image editing model, TRELLIS2, PartField, GeoTransformer, SDF optimization), but inference latency, convergence failure rate, and computational costs per scene are not discussed.

strengths: Addresses an important and practical problem in 3D content creation and robot simulation (Sim2Real): generating interactive, multi-object compositional 3D scenes with independent, watertight geometries rather than fused monolithic meshes.

Well-designed hybrid pipeline that effectively bridges 2D/3D generative priors (image editing and feed-forward 3D reconstruction) with classical geometric registration (GeoTransformer, scale-aware ICP) and physics-aware SDF collision optimization.
The inclusion of a VLM-driven agentic feedback loop to detect geometric intersections and iteratively re-prompt the 2D generative model is a sensible approach for handling severe occlusions.
Comprehensive qualitative visualizations demonstrating successful handling of two-part and multi-part compositions across diverse everyday object categories.
The curation and promised release of a large-scale interactive 3D dataset containing over 8,300 scenes represents a valuable contribution to the community.
weaknesses: The quantitative evaluation is conducted on an extremely small test set of only 10 cases (Section 5.3). Given that the paper introduces a dataset of over 8,300 scenes, evaluating quantitative metrics (CLIP alignment, collision ratios) on only 10 instances undermines the statistical significance of the reported numbers.

Lacks a systematic quantitative ablation study isolating the contributions of key components, such as the OBB scale initialization, GeoTransformer global initialization, the SDF collision loss schedule, and the agentic VLM refinement iterations.

No runtime or computational cost analysis is provided. The pipeline involves multiple sequential heavy components per iteration (2D image editing, 3D feed-forward reconstruction via TRELLIS2, PartField segmentation, GeoTransformer, SDF computation, and VLM querying), which could be computationally expensive and time-consuming.

Writing and editorial polish issues, notably an incomplete sentence at the end of the abstract/introduction on page 2 ('The code will be released on') and recurring typos such as 'collsion-aware' on pages 2 and 4.

strengths: Clear problem motivation: generating geometrically compatible, articulated/interactive multi-object 3D scenes with separate components is an important problem for robot simulation (Sim2Real) and 3D digital content creation, where monolithic 3D asset generation falls short.

Well-structured training-free pipeline: reformulating compositional scene generation into an anchor-based global-to-local registration followed by SDF-based collision-aware optimization is a sound engineering approach that leverages existing 2D and 3D foundation models.

Agentic closed-loop concept: using multi-view cross-sectional rendering analyzed by a VLM to iteratively edit and regenerate complementary geometry provides an intuitive way to resolve severe occlusion and geometric mismatches that cannot be fixed by rigid transformation alone.
Creation of a large-scale compositional asset dataset (approx. 8,300 scenes claimed) which could be valuable to the community if made publicly available.
weaknesses: Critically insufficient quantitative evaluation: Section 5.3 explicitly states that quantitative evaluation is conducted on only 10 test cases. Given that the authors constructed an 8,300-scene dataset, reporting metrics (CLIP similarity and intersection ratios) on merely 10 curated samples is statistically inadequate and does not rigorously demonstrate generalizability or robustness.

Lack of thorough ablation studies: the paper does not quantitatively isolate the contributions of key components, such as: (1) GeoTransformer initialization vs. standard ICP / bounding box alignment, (2) the role of the soft repulsion term versus the hard penalty in the SDF collision loss, and (3) the quantitative impact, convergence rate, and failure rate of the VLM-based agentic refinement loop across a sizable evaluation set.

Fragility and compounded errors in the multi-stage cascaded pipeline: the framework chains 2D generative image editing (Nano Banana Pro), single-image 3D reconstruction (TRELLIS2), 3D part segmentation (PartField), point registration (GeoTransformer/ICP), and VLM feedback. Errors at any intermediate stage (e.g., PartField structural artifacts, view inconsistency, or reconstruction hallucination under occlusion) directly degrade the guidance mesh and propagate downstream.

Limited physical plausibility beyond collision avoidance: the SDF loss penalizes intersection and enforces a safety margin, but it does not account for physical stability, resting contact, or gravity/friction support. Objects risk floating slightly above surfaces or being in unstable equilibria, which weakens the claim of generating simulation-ready assets for robotics.

Incomplete baseline comparison: while comparing against Jigsaw and 2BY2, these methods were not designed with scale optimization. Meanwhile, closely related contemporary work cited in the paper (e.g., Copy-Transform-Paste [7], which specifically performs VLM- and geometry-guided pairwise alignment) is not compared against quantitatively.
